title: Pitfalls & pro-tips: quadratics with complex roots

board_content.text: Traps to avoid, shortcuts to keep
$D<0$ never means 'no roots' — over $\mathbb{C}$ there are always two.
Apply the conjugate-root theorem ONLY when coefficients are real.
A complex number has two square roots; fix the branch by $\operatorname{sgn}(xy)=\operatorname{sgn}(b)$.
Pro-tip: check $D$ first — it names the root type before any computation.

segments_english.text: Let's close the subtopic with the traps that cost marks and the shortcuts that save them.
The biggest trap: a negative discriminant never means no roots. Over the complex numbers a quadratic always has exactly two roots. Declaring no solution when D is negative is simply wrong now.
Second: apply the conjugate-root theorem only when the coefficients are real. With complex coefficients the roots need not be conjugates, as we just saw.
Third: when D is negative, remember root D equals i times root of the size of D. Dropping that i is the recurring sign-flip error.
Fourth: a complex number always has two square roots. Get the branch right by making the sign of the product x y match the sign of b.
Fifth: Vieta's sum of roots is minus b over a, not plus b over a. That stray minus sign trips people up constantly.
Now the pro-tips. Always check the discriminant first; it names the type of roots before you compute anything, and with real coefficients you only need to find one complex root.

And keep this shortcut ready: to build a real quadratic from a complex root p plus i q, write x squared minus two p x plus p squared plus q squared equals zero. Sum is two p, product is p squared plus q squared.

segments_hinglish.text: Subtopic ko band karte hain un traps ke saath jo marks le jaate hain aur un shortcuts ke saath jo bachate hain.
Sabse bada trap: negative discriminant ka matlab kabhi no roots nahi hota. Complex numbers par quadratic ke hamesha theek do roots hote hain. D negative hone par no solution kehna ab bas galat hai.
Doosra: conjugate-root theorem sirf tab apply karo jab coefficients real hon. Complex coefficients ke saath roots conjugates hone zaroori nahi, jaisa abhi dekha.
Teesra: jab D negative ho, yaad rakho root D barabar i times root of the size of D. Wo i chhodna recurring sign-flip error hai.
Chautha: complex number ke hamesha do square roots hote hain. Branch sahi karo product x y ka sign b ke sign se match karke.
Paanchva: Vieta ka sum of roots hai minus b over a, plus b over a nahi. Wo bhatka minus sign logon ko lagataar phansaata hai.
Ab pro-tips. Hamesha discriminant pehle check karo; ye kuch bhi compute karne se pehle root type bata deta hai, aur real coefficients ke saath aapko sirf ek complex root nikaalna hota hai.

Aur ye shortcut ready rakho: complex root p plus i q se real quadratic banane ke liye likho x squared minus two p x plus p squared plus q squared equals zero. Sum hai two p, product hai p squared plus q squared.
